content:
anya: Quick follow-up from the attr handling RFC. Decision point: aggressive attr eviction at gateway vs per-tenant partitioning. short thoughts?

mike: Eviction wins on ops & cost. Partitioning gives fidelity for billing but multiplies shards.

tariq: We've hit support cases when billing.customer_id got evicted. Thats unacceptable for hot customers.

lucy: Noisy tenants (high-cardinality attrs) cause downstream query blowups. Dedicated partitions limit that blast radius.

anya: Ops note: partitioning makes autoscaling per-tenant unless we cap, which could increase cost dramatically.

mike: Proposal: hybrid. Keep a tiny pinned attr set at gateway, evict others; route top-N noisy tenants into dedicated partitions.

tariq: Suggested pinned attrs: ["billing.customer_id","billing.key","tenant.id","service.name","env"]. Enforce at proto-level; flag rather than drop when missing.

lucy: Add a soft-flag for missing pinned attrs so we can surface issues without losing traces. Also add max_extra_attrs to bound cardinality.

anya: Gateway config sketch: `pinned_attrs=5, max_extra_attrs=25, missing_policy=flag`, routing: `partition_threshold_tps=1500, dedicated_top_n=25`.

mike: For routing key use tenant.id + billing.key. Cross-partition queries: support admin fanout+merge, avoid for low-latency SLO paths.

ingest-bot: spike request created by @anya -> obs/ingest/evict-partition-spike (link: https://phab.redwood/EVCT-999).

anya: Next steps: mike+tariq 3-day spike to prototype pinned attr enforcement + soft-flagging, plus top-25 noisy tenant routing. Lucy will produce billing evals. I'll update RFC after spike.

lucy: I'll run attribution checks and post false-negative numbers in the thread.

mike: ack, will post results here. :thumbsup:
